name: LME49880 (National / TI Overture E-Series dual JFET-input audio op-amp)
tagline: National's late Overture E-Series JFET dual (7 nV/√Hz, 0.00003% THD+N). It came only in PSOP, is now obsolete, and Japanese op-amp rollers run it on DIP adapters.
technology: Dual JFET-input audio op-amp from National's LME 'Overture E-Series' (siblings: LME49720, LME49860, LME49990). The datasheet says the JFET process was used to lower flicker noise and the noise corner frequency. Supply range is ±5 V to ±17 V. It is unity-gain stable, drives capacitive loads up to 100 pF, and has typical input bias of 5 pA. The only package is an 8-lead PSOP with an exposed pad (MR suffix; TI's package addendum calls it 'SO PowerPAD').

part_numbers.notes: Generic dual. No single, quad or vendor DIP version has been seen. TI discontinued it as part of a process-technology end-of-life and names OPA1642 as the replacement (TI E2E thread 565578, about 2016-2017).

Lead-free orderable in the 8-lead PSOP with exposed pad. A 2014 package-option addendum listed it as ACTIVE ('SO PowerPAD', 8 pins); it is now OBSOLETE (TrustedParts, TI E2E). Whether a tape-and-reel MRX/NOPB version existed is unconfirmed.

Base National part/marking for the PSOP-8 package. The pre-/NOPB (leaded) orderable was not separately confirmed. Third-party shops (diyinhk 'LME49880 DIP Version'; reportedly Kyoritsu/eleshop EA8411, Digit, Bispa) sell it pre-mounted on DIP-8 adapter boards. Those are not TI part numbers.

lineage.notes: Introduced as the 'LME49880 Overture E-Series Dual JFET Input Audio Operational Amplifier'. The original datasheet date is December 2009, as printed in the SNAS455C header.

Came to TI with National in 2011. The datasheet was re-issued as SNAS455C (revised April 2013). TI later discontinued it as part of a process-technology end-of-life, with a lifetime-buy period, and recommends OPA1642 as the replacement. No die change under the same part number was found.

reputation.summary: A niche part, discussed mostly in the Japanese op-amp-rolling community and in an early diyAudio thread. Japanese users reportedly call it tight, clean and high-resolution, with a 'rich NatSemi tone'. It exists only in PSOP-8, so shops sell it pre-mounted on DIP-8 adapter boards: diyinhk's 'LME49880 DIP Version' is confirmed, and Kyoritsu/eleshop, Digit and Bispa reportedly do the same. The Japanese review and Q&A pages were not re-read, so the sonic claims are unverified folklore. No independent measurements (ASR, Samuel Groner) were found. The datasheet figures (7 nV/√Hz, 0.00003% THD+N) back its reputation as a low-distortion JFET part.
typical_uses: Op-amp swapping in DACs (I/V and output/LPF stages) via a DIP-8 adapter board
Op-amp swapping in headphone amps and preamps with DIP-8 sockets
Designed for high-fidelity audio preamp/filter stages (datasheet positioning)
caveats: PSOP-8 with exposed pad only. Socketed use needs a third-party DIP adapter, whose layout, decoupling and exposed-pad connection can affect results. Which supply rail the pad must connect to is not yet confirmed.
The part is obsolete at TI (process-technology end-of-life). Supply is now old stock, broker stock or adapter boards, and prices and counterfeit risk rise accordingly.
The praise is subjective and comes from a small, mostly Japanese community whose pages were not re-read. No independent measurements were found.

revision_history.changes: Initial release. The date comes from the original-date field of the SNAS455C header. The National-era copy is probably the alldatasheet NSC 394354 entry (unconfirmed).
The 'SNAS455B' designation was seen in a search summary of mirrored copies. The date and change text were not captured. Revision A is implied but was not seen.

Printed header: 'DECEMBER 2009 – REVISED APRIL 2013'. This is probably TI's April 2013 batch conversion of National LME datasheets to TI format; siblings LME49710 SNAS376C, LME49721 SNAS371C and LME49740 SNAS377B carry the same REVISED APRIL 2013 date. The exact change text was not seen, and no silicon change is implied.

A search summary said 'an earlier version of the datasheet, SNAS455B, was dated April 22, 2010'. The summary did not say which copy this came from. The top results were the kyohritsu, digikey.nl, partsconnexion SEMI-76009 and alldatasheet NSC 394354 copies, and the partsconnexion copy is the most likely holder. The change text was not shown. The date falls in the National era, before the 2011 TI acquisition. Revision A is implied, with a date between December 2009 and April 2010, but it was not seen.

counterfeit_notes: No LME49880-specific counterfeit reports were found. TI has obsoleted the part (process-technology end-of-life, about 2016-2017), so any 'new' stock is old inventory, broker stock or pre-mounted DIP adapter boards. Genuine parts come in an 8-lead PSOP with an exposed thermal pad on the underside. A plain SOIC-8 body with no pad, marked LME49880, is a red flag, although the pad is hidden once the chip is soldered to an adapter. Check that the top marking and date code fit the National (2009-2011) or TI era, and buy from reputable shops.

refuted_claims: Lifecycle status 'unknown' / possibly available: refuted. LME49880MR/NOPB is OBSOLETE (TI process-technology end-of-life), with OPA1642 named as the replacement.
Discovery hint 'SOIC-only': not accurate. The package is an 8-lead PSOP with an exposed pad (TI package addendum: 'SO PowerPAD'), not a plain SOIC. 'Surface-mount only, no DIP' still holds.

revision_chain_notes:
National/TI SNAS455 (LME49880 datasheet), oldest to newest:
(1) Original National edition, December 2009. The date comes from the original-date field of the SNAS455C header. The likely copy is the National-era alldatasheet NSC 394354 entry (14 pages, 502 KB), but its revision letter was not shown. MISSING: a copy confirmed to be the original edition.
(2) SNAS455A. Implied only; no date, copy or change text was found. MISSING.
(3) SNAS455B, dated April 22, 2010 (National era). New this round: the date appeared in a search summary that did not say which copy it came from. The partsconnexion SEMI-76009 PDF (listed as 'possibly B') is still the most likely copy, but the snippet did not tie the date to it. MISSING: a confirmed copy and the change text.
(4) SNAS455C, 'DECEMBER 2009 – REVISED APRIL 2013', the TI-format re-issue. Current ti.com symlink, kyohritsu and digikey copies. Change text not seen.
No revisions after C were found. The part is obsolete, with OPA1642 as the recommended replacement. No second sources exist.
New mirror URLs this round, all with the revision not shown: datasheetarchive.com index, electronicsdatasheets.com TI part page, alldatasheet.net copy of TI entry 841156.
Archive seed: I added only the http form of the known TI symlink. The legacy National URL (www.national.com/ds/LM/...) was never seen in any result, so I left it out of the seed list instead of guessing it. A Wayback lookup of national.com's LME49880 datasheet/product-folder paths is the best remaining route to editions A and B.
